lesson_title: The Buried Saucer: South Africa's Platinum Vault
hook_text: Most of the planet's platinum sits in one buried saucer under the bushveld.
clip_script: Deep beneath the bushveld lies a colossal, ancient saucer of once-molten rock — the Bushveld Igneous Complex. As it cooled, its minerals settled into flat bands, the way silt settles in a still dam — and two of those bands, the Merensky Reef and the UG2, are loaded with platinum. The saucer's rim breaks the surface in three arcs, and the mines queue up along them, with Rustenburg the capital of platinum country. Nearly every petrol and diesel vehicle on earth carries a pinch of this metal in its exhaust to scrub the fumes.
visual_style: Cutaway of a vast layered saucer beneath the veld, three arcs glowing at the rim, camera diving from Rustenburg headgear down a one-metre reef and up into a car's exhaust.
pacing: Slow reveal of the saucer, quick snap to the world market, strong close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — four ingredients, the hindering factors, and how to catch a mine on any map.
